atoms.label: browsers warn the user before they navigate to a malicious URL
storing the whole database of malicious URLs locally is infeasible for most users
sending every visited URL to an external service exposes the user's browsing
browsers use a Bloom filter as a local proxy for queries to the external database
a Bloom filter has no false negatives
a Bloom filter has a low false positive rate
the widely cited expression (1 - (1 - 1/m)^(kn))^k is the false positive rate of a Bloom filter
the Bloom filter's behaviour has been the subject of 30 years of contention and corrections
the authors have a certified (Coq/Rocq) proof of the false positive rate of a Bloom filter
a query can return a positive result for a value never inserted (false positives are possible)
the hash functions and their outputs are modelled as random and independent
the probability that a given bit is raised after n insertions is 1 - (1 - 1/m)^(kn)
the k bits a query checks are independent of one another
the k bits the hash functions select are always distinct
Bose et al.'s balls-into-bins expression is the false positive rate
Bose et al.'s derivation is free of errors
no further errors will be found in the certified derivation
the mechanisation yielded a few novel data structures
in practice browsers send a hash of the URL, not the URL itself
the asymptotic behaviour of Bloom's bound agrees with the corrected expression
the first version of the authors' work was rejected by reviewers who rediscovered Bose et al.'s error
Bloom himself introduced the error in the derivation presented as his

vocab.label: Browsers protect privacy with a Bloom filter as a local proxy
The widely cited false positive rate is wrong; we certified the true one
What a Bloom filter is: no false negatives, but false positives
Bloom's derivation, step by step: the single-bit probability is right
The bits are not independent, so the final step fails
Bose et al. notice the error and correct it, with errors of their own
Ceramist certifies the corrected bound from first principles
What the post leaves out, and where to read more
